result.title: Beyond Distribution Matching: Selective Margin Preservation for Supervised Fine-Tuning
result.summary: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) changes logit margins among non-target tokens at teacher-forced prefixes. Matching a local reference distribution keeps those probabilities and also penalizes margin expansions. We ask whether a soft auxiliary can preserve selected local non-target margin relations without freezing that distribution. We introduce \textbf{Selective Rank-Preserving SFT (SRP-SFT)}, a soft margin target: a hinge on reference-scaled lower bounds for pairs from the reference's top-$K$ non-target tokens, applied at fixed teacher-forced prefixes. The hinge stops once the requested bound is met. We derive the KL cost of violating a margin, characterize the feasible region and its conditional utility, and give a finite-step condition for reducing aggregate violations. In one-epoch experiments on Qwen3-4B-Base and UltraFeedback, this target raises MATH-500 and code-generation scores over CE and LP-SFT at all three training seeds. At seed 1234, MATH-500 pass@1 rises from 49.56\% to 54.56\% and the four-metric code mean rises from 65.91\% to 69.50\% relative to LP-SFT. Ranking controls, held-out cache diagnostics, sensitivity sweeps, and six additional backbones show where these score changes appear.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Selective Rank-Preserving SFT（SRP-SFT）：在 teacher-forced 前缀上，用 hinge 对参考模型 top-K 非目标 token 的 margin 下界施加软约束，并分析违反 margin 的 KL 代价与可行域；在 Qwen3-4B-Base 与 UltraFeedback 上报告 MATH-500 和代码生成分数优于 CE 与 LP-SFT。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文属纯文本训练期正则化，不直接研究多模态推理；其「选择性保留非目标 token 相对 margin 关系」的监督设计，可能可供核查 LVR 微调时如何保留内部状态中的关系结构、缓解信息坍缩。
